deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It holds two non-mathematical drafts, and the faint numeral columns are bleed-through.

(a) Upper left: a column of names, apparently a mailing list. As read it gives Dedekind, Schering, a doubtful name with 'Brünn?' beside it, Göbel?, Müller?, Brauns? 'zu Zürich?', Selling, Lindemann?, and one more doubtful name. Some readings are suspect. Dedekind, Schering and Selling all fit Riemann's Göttingen circle around 1859–66. The facing page carries an offprint dedication, 'Herrn Tschebyschew ... hochachtungsvoll der Verfasser'. So this list is most plausibly the recipients of offprints of a paper, probably the 1859 prime-number memoir. That is my inference.

(b) A German letter draft, worked over several times, opening 'Sehr geehrter Herr', with an abandoned salutation 'Mein lieber Herr ...' above it. In substance: a Professor (name unclear) has passed on to me your letter and warmly recommended its enclosure. A first ending, 'ich bin daher mit Vergnügen bereit, Ihre Wünsche nach Möglichkeit zu erfüllen', is struck out. It is replaced by: I was pleased to make the acquaintance of so striving and talented a mathematician and am glad to give you the information you asked for ('die gewünschten Nachweisungen'). 'Hochachtungsvoll' follows. A new paragraph then begins: 'Seit dem Anfang der vierziger Jahre (wo ich ...) habe ich ... schon bemerkt ...' and breaks off.

The bundle is 'Primzahlen'. The previous page holds trial divisions of 6082613 and Pell/√2 convergents; the next page holds the Tschebyschew dedication and series for the exponential integral. So the reply plausibly concerns prime-number questions. If the writer is Riemann, 'since the beginning of the 1840s' would refer to his Lüneburg Gymnasium years. He is reported to have read Legendre's Théorie des nombres then. The parenthesis may name that circumstance, but this is speculation; the words are illegible.

(c) The mirror-image decimal columns faintly visible in the middle and lower part (0,0000..., 1,7182818..., etc.) are show-through from the verso. That verso carries the series tables for e^1−1, e^2 and Σx^n/(n!·n).

No derivation is present to reconstruct.

results.what: Draft reply letter to a young mathematician, recommended by a professor, promising requested references or information. It includes an autobiographical remark that the writer has been concerned with or noticed something (presumably about primes) since the early 1840s.
List of names (Dedekind, Schering, Selling, ...), probably offprint recipients

deep.surprise_reason: The page has no mathematical content. The only point of possible interest is biographical: a claim of interest dating to the early 1840s, if the letter is Riemann's and concerns primes. It is consistent with the known story of his reading Legendre at school. It is a minor archival detail.

transcription_corrections: The faint reversed numeral columns (0,0000..., 1,7182818..., etc.) are bleed-through from the verso (the next page's exponential-series tables). They are not text on this page.
The '66' at the right margin is the folio number, not mathematics.
The fragments along the left edge belong to the adjoining leaf, not this page.
The name list is largely uncertain; in particular 'Lindemann' is doubtful.

In the letter, the struck passages are 'ich bin daher mit Vergnügen bereit' and 'Ihre Wünsche nach Möglichkeit zu erfüllen', and later 'Ihre Wünsche nach Möglichkeit'. The final text reads '... und ich bin mit Vergnügen bereit, Ihnen die gewünschten Nachweisungen zu geben.'
The last line reads 'Seit dem Anfang der vierziger Jahre (wo ich ...), habe ich ... schon ...'; the parenthesis and the end are not reliably legible.
